bull.b: Broad-based growth in viewership, social reach, and digital consumption strengthens Formula 1’s global audience asset. Greater engagement increases the value of media rights, sponsorship inventory, licensing, and premium experiences, supporting multiple durable monetization channels.

Sold-out hospitality products demonstrate strong demand for high-value experiences, while international media growth shows expanding commercial reach. New premium offerings, licensing agreements, and retail expansion can deepen revenue per fan and diversify Formula 1’s earnings base.

bull.t: Strong cash generation and balance sheet
bull.b: Robust operating and free cash flow provides resources to fund investments, service obligations, and pursue growth without relying heavily on new equity. Combined with very low debt-to-equity, this supports financial resilience and gives management meaningful capital allocation flexibility.

bear.b: The recent decline in revenue and lower net income indicate that reported earnings remain sensitive to timing and operating conditions. This volatility can make results less predictable, reduce the visibility of near-term profit growth, and complicate sustained reinvestment planning.

Although liquidity and covenant compliance provide support, the sizable debt load and 3.4x net leverage create ongoing obligations against operating cash flow. Leverage can restrict financial flexibility, increase sensitivity to weaker earnings, and limit the funds available for other strategic priorities.

A large share of pre-team-share adjusted OIBDA is allocated to teams, limiting the portion retained by the commercial rights holder. Even with management expecting improvement for the full year, this structural cost burden constrains margin capture and operating leverage.
